data.long_meaning: The one who is noble, generous, and kind. A good-natured person who is kind to everyone around them. Parents who choose Raumaan usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raumaan suggests a person of high moral character, someone who embodies the virtues of nobility, generosity, and kindness. In Islamic culture, these qualities are highly valued and celebrated. A person named Raumaan is expected to treat others with compassion and respect, offering assistance and support when needed. They are expected to be magnanimous in their dealings with people, contrary to the harshness and hardheartedness that may prevail in society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Raumaan serves as a reminder to uphold the values of noble character and virtuous behavior. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "Verily, Allah loves those who are generous in this world, so He is generous to them in the hereafter." (Bukhari and Muslim). Thus, the name Raumaan not only serves as a source of inspiration to embody noble character but also carries the potential to draw Allah's mercy and blessings in the hereafter by consistently practicing generosity and kindness.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, vol. 11, p. 117-118. Raumaan ibn Zayd was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who was known for his generosity and piety. He was one of the ten companions given the title 'As-Sahabah ar-Raqiqoon' (the Constant Companions) due to their uninterrupted company with the Prophet (PBUH). Raumaan was also known as 'Abu Hurairah Al-Ansari', and was a native of Damascus.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic History, Companions of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)

historical_references.reference: Ibn Ishaq's Sirah Rasul Allah, p. 689. Raumaan ibn Zayd al-Ghifari was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who was known for his love and devotion towards the Prophet (PBUH). He was one of the first converts to Islam and was also known as 'Abu Hurairah Al-Ansari'. Raumaan was a very humble and pious man, and it is reported that he would often sleep in the mosque and offer the night prayers alongside the Prophet (PBUH). He was also known for his memory and would often narrate the sayings and actions of the Prophet (PBUH) to the Muslim community.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic History, Companions of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Hadith
